The test image shows two bell peppers with large, dark brown to black sunken lesions covering most of the fruit surface. The lesions show distinct concentric rings and appear leathery/firm. Key features:
- Affected part: **fruit (pod)**
- Large dark (near-black) sunken lesions
- Concentric ring patterns
- Leathery texture

Top candidates: **Phytophthora_Blight** (large dark fruit lesions, leathery) and **Anthracnose** (concentric ring sunken lesions on fruit).

Let me view the Phytophthora_Blight pod reference:

The Phytophthora_Blight reference shows wrinkled/collapsed peppers with lighter, non-concentric lesions — very different from the test image.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: two peppers with large, very dark (near-black) sunken lesions showing clear **concentric rings**, leathery texture
- Phytophthora Blight: collapsed wrinkled fruit with diffuse lighter discoloration — does NOT match
- **Anthracnose** KB description: "concentric ring pattern with tan center and dark specks; water-soaked and sunken lesions expanding; dark fungal structures in center; lesions darken progressively" — matches perfectly with the dark concentric ring pattern on fruit

The concentric rings, very dark (almost black) coloring, and sunken fruit lesions are the hallmark of Anthracnose on pepper/tomato fruit.
